newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to auction port terminal rights by year-end.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to auction port terminal rights by year-end.

text.p: Mexico plans to hold an auction for the rights to operate the port terminal at Puerto Vallarta in the state of Jalisco before the end of the year, a port official said Tuesday.
Roberto Hernandez Camallich, director of Puerto Vallarta's port authority, said the cost of operating the port would be about 20 million pesos a year.
Currently, most Mexican ports are operated by the government, although privatizations begun in August 1994 have put some of the larger terminals in private hands.
The concession to operate the Puerto Vallarta terminal will offer exclusive operating rights for 25 years.

An auction later this year would mark the second attempt to privatize the port. Last December, Transportacion Maritima Mexicana (TMM) won the bidding only to have it revoked after the company also won the concession to operate the port in Acapulco, Guerrero.
Mexican competition laws forced TMM to decide which of the two terminals it would operate.
The Jalisco port is the second-largest tourist port in Mexico, with revenue of more than 1.5 million pesos in the first half of 1996, a 30.7 percent increase from the same period the previous year.
